page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-32-lssd is a general-purpose server type built on the x86_64 processor architecture. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs and 124.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not feature graphical processing units, focusing strictly on standard central processing workloads.

Integrated local storage is a key specification for this machine type, supplying 805 GB of total capacity across two local NVMe SSDs. This low-latency solid-state storage operates directly within the host system. Standard networking does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured network routing or Cloud NAT for external access.

The provision of dedicated CPU cores ensures consistent computational throughput without thread contention. Incorporating local NVMe storage provides strong resource density for disk-intensive workflows compared to configurations relying exclusively on remote persistent disks. Because local NVMe storage is ephemeral, workloads require external redundancy configurations to manage data persistence risks.

Given its balanced ratio of processing capacity to memory and fast local disk access, the c4d-standard-32-lssd is well suited for database engines requiring scratch space or fast write buffers, continuous integration build clusters, batch processing, and transactional enterprise applications.

The instance omits GPU accelerators, prioritizing standard compute execution. A key physical asset is the inclusion of 805 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across two drives, minimizing latency for disk operations directly on the host. Networking provisions do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With dedicated core scheduling, the system avoids multi-tenant compute contention, maintaining stable execution rates across demanding multi-threaded tasks. This hardware profile provides favorable resource density for throughput-dependent applications, making the server suitable for operational databases requiring fast caching layers, data ingestion pipelines, container nodes, and large-scale software compilation environments.
